2027-06-09.title: Wednesday of the third week after Pentecost
readings: They exchanged the truth about God for a lie
“I am the resurrection and the life. Do you believe this?”
2027-06-09.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Third Sunday after Pentecost.
2027-06-09.verse: I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live
theo: The Epistle today is one of the hardest pages St Paul ever wrote, and it is wise to read it whole, in its place. Paul is beginning his letter to the Romans by showing that the whole human race needs the Gospel. The root of all that goes wrong, he says, is not first a bad deed but a false worship: “they exchanged the truth about God for a lie and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever! Amen.” When God is pushed out of the centre, something else is put there: pleasure, money, power, the self. And three times Paul repeats a frightening phrase: “God gave them up.” God does not need to send a thunderbolt. He respects our choice and lets us have what we have chosen, and the choice bears its own fruit. A heart that will not acknowledge God slowly loses its sense of what is true and good, in the body, in the mind and in every relationship. St Augustine saw this in his own youth: he had looked for beauty and joy in created things instead of in the One who made them, and found only restlessness (Confessions 10.27, in substance).

Among the fruits of that exchange Paul names sexual acts between persons of the same sex. The Church, faithful to the word of God, teaches that such acts are contrary to the Creator's plan and can never be approved, because the gift of sexuality belongs within the faithful marriage of a man and a woman, open to life (Catechism 2357). But we must not stop reading there, as if this page were about other people. Paul's list goes on: “They were filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, covetousness, malice. Full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, craftiness, they are gossips, slanderers, God-haters, insolent, haughty, boastful, inventors of evil, rebellious toward parents, foolish, faithless, heartless, ruthless.” Gossip, envy, boasting, disobedience to parents: there is no one in the church this morning who is not somewhere on this list. And the very next sentence of the letter, which we do not read today, turns on the reader: “Therefore you have no excuse, whoever you are, when you judge others.” The Catechism asks us to receive every person who carries this struggle with respect, compassion and sensitivity, avoiding every sign of unjust discrimination (Catechism 2358), and it calls every one of us, beginning with ourselves, to chastity and conversion (Catechism 2348, 2359). Paul writes this dark chapter only so that the light of chapter 3 may shine: all have sinned, and all may be justified by God's grace through faith in Christ.

The Gospel brings that light into a house of mourning. Lazarus has been in the tomb four days; Bethany is full of neighbours, “many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them about their brother”, a tender picture of a community that shows up for a funeral, as our Kerala villages still do. Martha goes out to meet Jesus with grief and faith mixed together: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. But even now I know that God will give you whatever you ask of him.” Jesus answers with one of the greatest sentences in the Gospel: “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live, and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?” And Martha, standing near the tomb, makes a confession as full as Peter's: “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.” Here is the answer to Romans 1. The human heart that exchanged the Creator for creatures ends in the tomb; but the Creator has come to the tomb in person. Whatever has died in us, whatever we have exchanged and lost, the Lord who stands at Lazarus's grave says to us too: even now. In every Holy Qurbono we pray for our departed, and we receive the One who is the resurrection and the life.
outline: Ask: what have I put at the centre of my life in the place that belongs to God?
Worshipping the creature rather than the Creator, and the meaning of “God gave them up”.
Point 2 · A list that includes all of us
Gossip, envy and boasting stand beside graver sins; no one may judge.
Martha's faith at the tomb, and Jesus, the resurrection and the life.
“I am the resurrection and the life. Do you believe this?”
live: Put God back in the centre (Romans 1:25)
Name to yourself one created thing, a phone, a habit, an ambition, that has crept into the place of God, and give the first minutes of tomorrow morning to prayer instead.
Bring to Jesus one situation you have given up on, in your family or in yourself, and pray: Lord, even now.
2027-06-09.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you are the resurrection and the life. Too often we exchange the truth about God for a lie and serve created things rather than the Creator; forgive us, and do not give us up to ourselves. Take from us the sins of the tongue and of the heart, gossip, envy, pride and every disorder of the body, and give us clean hearts. When we stand before the tombs of our hopes and of our loved ones, give us Martha's faith to say: even now. Raise us to new life, and bring our departed into the light of your face. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the altar the Creator gives himself to his creatures: in the Holy Qurbono we receive the risen Lord, the resurrection and the life, and the medicine that heals hearts turned away from God.

quick: Paul shows that when people exchange the truth about God for a lie and worship creatures, every part of life becomes disordered.
His list of sins includes gossip, envy, boasting and disobedience to parents, so that no one may judge others; all need God's grace.
At the tomb of Lazarus, Jesus tells Martha: “I am the resurrection and the life,” and she confesses him as the Messiah, the Son of God.
2027-06-09.action: Give the first ten minutes of tomorrow to God before you touch your phone.
2027-06-09.question: What created thing have I quietly put in the place of God?

family.explain: Martha and Mary were very sad because their brother Lazarus had died. Their neighbours came to comfort them. When Jesus came, Martha ran to meet him. She said: if you had been here, my brother would not have died. Jesus told her: I am the resurrection and the life. That means that Jesus is stronger than death, and those who love him will live with him for ever.
family.intention: We pray for the members of our family who have died, and for families who are sad because someone has died.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom do we miss who has gone to God? Let us say a prayer for that person now.”

illus: In a parish near Pathanamthitta a young father died in a road accident during the monsoon, leaving his wife and two small children. At the funeral the house was full; neighbours of every faith had come, as they do in Kerala, and sat on the verandah in the rain. When the priest read the Gospel of Lazarus, the young widow, who had not spoken all day, said Martha's words aloud after him: Yes, Lord, I believe. Months later she told the parish women's group that she still did not understand why it had happened, but that those words had held her up like a hand under her arm. She said: I could not say that everything was all right. I could only say, even now, I believe.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, resurrection and life, turn our hearts back from every idol to the living God, and give us faith to say with Martha: even now. Amen.
share: They exchanged the truth about God for a lie (Romans 1:25). What lies about God or about myself have I believed?
Gossips, slanderers, boastful, rebellious toward parents (Romans 1:29–30). Which of these words touches my own life?
I am the resurrection and the life. Do you believe this? (John 11:25–26). What would change in me if I truly believed it?
pm.resp: Lord, I believe; raise us to life.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the truth about God with courage and receive every sinner with mercy.
For all who are caught in addictions and disorders of body or mind, that they may find healing and new life.
For those who gossip, envy and judge, ourselves first, that we may be given clean hearts.
For families who mourn, especially those who have lost someone suddenly, that they may be comforted by neighbours and by hope.
For our departed, that they may rise with Christ.
pm.close: Father, Creator of all, we have often served created things instead of you. Forgive us, turn us back to you, and through your Son, the resurrection and the life, raise us and our departed to the life that never ends. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul shows us today what happens when people turn away from God: they exchanged the truth about God for a lie and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator (Romans 1:25). When God is not at the centre, something else takes his place, and life slowly falls into disorder.

Paul's list of sins is long, and it includes all of us: gossips, slanderers, boastful, rebellious toward parents (Romans 1:29–30). We must not read this page and think of other people. Paul says in the next chapter: you have no excuse, whoever you are, when you judge others (Romans 2:1). We all need mercy.

And mercy comes. In the Gospel Jesus stands at the tomb of Lazarus. Martha says: even now I know that God will give you whatever you ask of him (John 11:22). Jesus answers: I am the resurrection and the life (John 11:25). He asks her, and he asks us: Do you believe this?

Let us answer with Martha: Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God (John 11:27). Whatever has died in us, whatever we have lost by turning away, Jesus can raise. Let us put him back at the centre today, and let us trust him with our departed. Amen.
kids: Children, sometimes people love things more than they love God: toys, phones, money. St Paul says that when we put things in God's place, everything goes wrong. In the Gospel, Jesus' friend Lazarus had died, and his sister Martha was crying. Jesus told her: I am the resurrection and the life. Jesus is stronger than death! Let us always keep Jesus in the first place in our hearts, and he will keep us safe for ever.

intro: Theme: “I am the resurrection and the life. Do you believe this?”
On Wednesday of the third week after Pentecost: the exchange of the Creator for creatures, a list of sins that includes us all, and Martha's faith at the tomb.

sub: “God gave them up”: our choices bear fruit.
Restless until the heart returns to its Maker.
q: for my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and dug out cisterns for themselves, cracked cisterns that can hold no water.
Little children, keep yourselves from idols.
points.apply: Remove or limit one thing this week that has begun to take God's place in your day.

points.h: A list that includes all of us
sub: Disorders of the body and sins of the tongue side by side.
Respect, compassion and the call to conversion for all.
q: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and put a new and right spirit within me.
Therefore you have no excuse, whoever you are, when you judge others
points.apply: For one day, say nothing about anyone who is not present, unless it is good.

points.h: “Even now”: the resurrection and the life
sub: The Creator comes to the tomb.
q: I am going to open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people
But in fact Christ has been raised from the dead, the first fruits of those who have died.
points.apply: Visit or call a family that has lost someone in the past year, and pray for their departed at the next Holy Qurbono.

concl: When the Creator is exchanged for creatures, life falls into disorder; none of us is outside that story.
But the Creator has come to our tombs, and he says to every dead hope: even now.
2027-06-09.resolve: Put God back at the centre, judge no one, and answer Jesus with Martha: Yes, Lord, I believe.
